title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Early Recognition and Developmental Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Children and young people under 19 with possible autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in primary care, paediatrics and child mental health: recognition by age, regression, referral, the diagnostic assessment, coexisting conditions and support while waiting. Uses NICE CG128 and CG170 and notes the Saudi Health Council 2023 national guideline.
findings: Rebuilt from the thin 21 Oct 2026 version: age-banded features, risk factors, regression rules, the 3-month assessment standard, assessment components, coexisting conditions and six management steps added.
Medicine plan stays 'no drug indicated' for recognition and referral; what not to prescribe for core features is listed from NICE CG170.
All statements trace to sources opened on 22 Oct 2026.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi Health Council 2023 autism guideline exists but its full text could not be opened (registration-gated); its screening tools and timelines are not included.
Normal values for developmental checks are descriptive; no numeric screening cut-offs are given.
Distinguishing features for differentials are summarised from the NICE CG128 differential list; the one-line features are clinical descriptions.

pathophysiology.summary: Autism is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition of differences in reciprocal social communication with restricted, repetitive behaviours and sensory differences (NICE CG128 Appendix, Boxes 2–4). It is more common with an autistic sibling, birth before 35 weeks, maternal valproate in pregnancy, intellectual disability, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and some genetic conditions (NICE CG128, Box 1). It may be under-recognised in girls and in verbally able children (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.2).
keyMechanisms: Reciprocal social communication differs from age expectations (NICE CG128 Appendix, Boxes 2–4).
Restricted interests, repetitive behaviour and insistence on sameness (NICE CG128 Appendix, Boxes 2–4).
Over- or under-reaction to sensory input (NICE CG128 Appendix, Boxes 2–4).
Higher prevalence with genetic disorders such as fragile X and tuberous sclerosis (NICE CG128, Box 1).

symptoms: Preschool: fewer than 10 words by age 2, or loss of words; echolalia (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 2).
Preschool: absent or late response to name with normal hearing (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 2).
School age: talks at people rather than conversing; takes language literally (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 3).
Secondary age: few close friendships; distress or aggression with change (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 4).
physicalSigns: Reduced social smiling, eye contact and pointing to share interest (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 2).
Hand flapping, rocking or spinning (NICE CG128 Appendix, Box 2).
Wood's light skin check for neurofibromatosis or tuberous sclerosis (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.6).
Dysmorphic features, macrocephaly or microcephaly; signs of injury or maltreatment (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.6).
redFlags: Regression in language or social skills under 3 years — refer to the autism team (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.1).
Language regression over 3 years, or motor regression at any age — refer first to a paediatrician or paediatric neurologist (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.2).
precipitants: Maternal sodium valproate in pregnancy (NICE CG128, Box 1).
Intellectual disability, ADHD, neonatal encephalopathy, Down's syndrome, fragile X, muscular dystrophy, neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis (NICE CG128, Box 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Language delay with intact social reciprocity and play (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.7).

differentials.condition: Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Social skills in line with overall developmental level (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.7).
Responses improve once the sensory deficit is addressed (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.7).
Developmental regression with neurological features (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.7).
Social difficulty linked to care history (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.7).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: ICD-11 or DSM-5 criteria applied in a multidisciplinary assessment (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.5).
Start the diagnostic assessment within 3 months of referral to the autism team (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.1).
Severity and duration, presence across settings, impact, parent concern, Box 1 factors and likelihood of another diagnosis (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Take the concern seriously
actions: Consider autism when development or behaviour raises concern; do not rule it out because box features are absent (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.2).
Ask about Box 1 risk factors (NICE CG128, Box 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Act on regression
actions: Under 3 years with language or social regression: refer to the autism team (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.1).
Over 3 years with language regression, or any motor regression: refer to a paediatrician or paediatric neurologist first (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer to the autism team
actions: Weigh severity, duration, settings, impact and parent concern (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.3.3).
Send developmental history and school information.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnostic assessment
actions: Multidisciplinary assessment with history, observation, examination, differential diagnosis, coexisting conditions and a strengths-and-needs profile (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.5).
No routine medical investigations (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.7.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Support while waiting and after
actions: Consider a play-based social-communication intervention involving parents, carers and teachers (NICE CG170, Recommendation 1.3.1).
Look for pain, physical illness, mental health problems, environment, routine change and abuse behind behaviour that challenges (NICE CG170, Recommendation 1.4.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Avoid unhelpful medicines
actions: Do not use antipsychotics, antidepressants, anticonvulsants or exclusion diets for core features (NICE CG170, Recommendation 1.3.2).
Antipsychotic for behaviour that challenges only by a paediatrician or psychiatrist; review at 3–4 weeks and stop if no response by 6 weeks (NICE CG170, Recommendations 1.4.10–1.4.11).
Sleep: medicine only if a sleep plan fails; melatonin after specialist advice (NICE CG170, Recommendation 1.7.7).

medicationPlan.note: Recognition and referral need no medicine. Do not prescribe antipsychotics, antidepressants, anticonvulsants, secretin, chelation or exclusion diets for core autism features (NICE CG170, Recommendations 1.3.2 and 1.6.4). Specialist-only options for behaviour that challenges and sleep are described in Management.

learningObjectives: Apply the NICE regression referral rules.
Know what not to prescribe for core features.
keyPoints: Assessment should start within 3 months of referral.
pitfalls: Waiting for every box feature before referring.
Ordering routine genetic tests or EEG without indication.

patientEducation: Explain why autism is being considered and what the assessment involves.
Give the family a named contact and expected timeline.
lifestyleAndDiet: Do not start gluten-free or casein-free diets for core features (NICE CG170, Recommendation 1.3.2).
Address feeding problems and restricted diets as coexisting conditions (NICE CG128, Recommendation 1.5.15).
dischargeCriteria: Not an acute condition; referral sent and accepted, family has a named contact.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track that assessment starts within 3 months of referral; review support needs, sleep, feeding and safeguarding while waiting.
